```{python}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

# Import libraries
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

from palmerpenguins import load_penguins

# Load dataset
penguins = load_penguins()

# Clean data
penguin_data = penguins.dropna(
    subset=["species", "island"]
).copy()

# Summary statistics
total_penguins = len(penguin_data)

total_species = penguin_data["species"].nunique()

# Most common species
top_species = (
    penguin_data["species"]
    .value_counts()
    .idxmax()
)

# Most populated island
top_island = (
    penguin_data["island"]
    .value_counts()
    .idxmax()
)

# Consistent Dark2 color palette
species_order = sorted(
    penguin_data["species"].unique()
)

palette = sns.color_palette(
    "Dark2",
    n_colors=len(species_order)
)

species_palette = dict(
    zip(species_order, palette)
)
```

## Row {height=20%}

### Total Penguins

```{python}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Total Penguins Observed"
#| color: primary

dict(value=total_penguins)
```

```{python}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Number of Species"
#| color: success

dict(value=total_species)
```

### Most Common Species

```{python}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Most Observed Species"
#| color: info

dict(value=top_species)
```

### Most Populated Island

```{python}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Island with Most Penguins"

dict(value=top_island)
```

## Row {height=80%}

### Species Distribution

```{python}
#| title: "Penguin Observations by Species"
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-width: 7

# Count penguins by species
species_counts = (
    penguin_data["species"]
    .value_counts()
    .reindex(species_order)
    .reset_index()
)

species_counts.columns = [
    "species",
    "count"
]

# Sort species by population
species_counts = species_counts.sort_values(
    "count",
    ascending=False
)

# Create chart
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4.5))

bars = ax.bar(
    species_counts["species"],
    species_counts["count"],
    color=[
        species_palette[species]
        for species in species_counts["species"]
    ],
    width=0.65
)

# Add data labels
ax.bar_label(
    bars,
    padding=5,
    fontsize=11
)

# Chart title and labels
ax.set_title(
    "Penguin Observations by Species",
    fontsize=14,
    pad=15
)

ax.set_xlabel("Penguin Species")
ax.set_ylabel("Number of Penguins")

# Remove unnecessary borders
ax.spines["top"].set_visible(False)
ax.spines["right"].set_visible(False)

# Add space above bars
ax.set_ylim(
    0,
    species_counts["count"].max() * 1.15
)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

**Interpretation**

Adelie penguins have the highest number of observations, with 152 penguins. Gentoo follows with 124 observations, while Chinstrap has the lowest count at 68.

### Island Distribution by Species

```{python}
#| title: "Penguin Distribution Across Islands"
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-width: 7

# Count penguins by island and species
island_counts = (
    penguin_data
    .groupby(["island", "species"])
    .size()
    .unstack(fill_value=0)
)

# Set species order
island_counts = island_counts.reindex(
    columns=species_order
)

# Create stacked bar chart
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4.5))

_ = island_counts.plot(
    kind="bar",
    stacked=True,
    ax=ax,
    color=[
        species_palette[species]
        for species in island_counts.columns
    ],
    width=0.65
)

# Add labels inside each bar
for container in ax.containers:

    labels = [
        str(int(value)) if value > 0 else ""
        for value in container.datavalues
    ]

    ax.bar_label(
        container,
        labels=labels,
        label_type="center",
        color="white",
        fontsize=10
    )

# Chart title and labels
ax.set_title(
    "Penguin Distribution Across Islands",
    fontsize=14,
    pad=15
)

ax.set_xlabel("Island")
ax.set_ylabel("Number of Penguins")

# Legend
ax.legend(
    title="Penguin Species",
    loc="upper center",
    bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.15),
    ncol=3,
    frameon=False
)

# Remove unnecessary borders
ax.spines["top"].set_visible(False)
ax.spines["right"].set_visible(False)

# Keep island labels horizontal
ax.tick_params(
    axis="x",
    labelrotation=0
)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

**Interpretation**

Biscoe Island has the highest penguin population (168 observations), followed by Dream Island (124) and Torgersen Island (52). Gentoo penguins are found on Biscoe, Chinstrap on Dream, and Adelie on all three islands.


# Statistical Analysis

This section examines penguin body mass across species and the relationship between penguin species and island. It includes descriptive summaries, statistical tests, effect size, and supporting visualizations.

```{python}
#| include: false
#| label: statistical-analysis-setup

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mtick
from scipy import stats
from statsmodels.stats.oneway import anova_oneway
from IPython.display import Markdown

# Ensure `data1` is loaded (e.g., data1 = sns.load_dataset("penguins"))

# Descriptive statistics for body mass by species
body_mass_clean = data1.dropna(subset=["species", "body_mass_g"])

body_mass_summary = (
    body_mass_clean.groupby("species", as_index=False)["body_mass_g"]
    .agg(
        Observations="count",
        Mean="mean",
        Median="median",
        **{"Standard Deviation": "std"},
        Minimum="min",
        Maximum="max",
    )
)

# Welch's one-way ANOVA compares mean body mass across species
welch_result = anova_oneway(
    body_mass_clean["body_mass_g"],
    body_mass_clean["species"],
    use_var="unequal",
)

# Chi-square test examines the association between species and island
species_island_data = data1.dropna(subset=["species", "island"])
species_island_table = pd.crosstab(
    species_island_data["species"], species_island_data["island"]
)

chi2_stat, chi2_pval, chi2_dof, _ = stats.chi2_contingency(
    species_island_table, correction=False
)

# Cramer's V measures the strength of the species-island association
n_total = species_island_table.to_numpy().sum()
min_dim = min(species_island_table.shape[0] - 1, species_island_table.shape[1] - 1)
cramers_v = np.sqrt(chi2_stat / (n_total * min_dim))

palette = {"Adelie": "#A8DADC", "Chinstrap": "#8296AB", "Gentoo": "#315F91"}
species_order = ["Adelie", "Chinstrap", "Gentoo"]
```

## Row {height=42%}

### Column

```{python}
#| title: "Body Mass Descriptive Statistics"
#| label: body-mass-descriptive-table

table1 = body_mass_summary.rename(
    columns={
        "species": "Species",
        "Mean": "Mean (g)",
        "Median": "Median (g)",
        "Standard Deviation": "SD (g)",
        "Minimum": "Minimum (g)",
        "Maximum": "Maximum (g)",
    }
).round(2)

Markdown(table1.to_markdown(index=False))
```

::: {.card .summary-card}
The table shows that Gentoo penguins have the highest average body mass at 5,076.02 grams, considerably heavier than Adelie and Chinstrap penguins, which have averages of 3,700.66 grams and 3,733.09 grams, respectively. Gentoo penguins also have the highest median body mass at 5,000 grams, while both Adelie and Chinstrap have a median of 3,700 grams. In terms of variation, Gentoo has the highest standard deviation at 504.12 grams, followed by Adelie at 458.57 grams and Chinstrap at 384.54 grams. Overall, the results indicate that Gentoo penguins are generally heavier, while Chinstrap penguins have the least variation in body mass.
:::

### Column

```{python}
#| title: "Inferential Statistics"
#| label: inferential-statistics-table

def format_pval(p, eps=0.001):
    return f"<{eps}" if p < eps else f"{p:.3g}"

inferential_summary = pd.DataFrame({
    "Test": ["Welch's one-way ANOVA", "Chi-square test", "Cramer's V"],
    "Statistic": [
        f"F = {welch_result.statistic:.3f}; df = {welch_result.df[0]:.2f}, {welch_result.df[1]:.2f}",
        f"X-squared = {chi2_stat:.3f}; df = {chi2_dof}",
        f"{cramers_v:.3f}",
    ],
    "P-value / Effect Size": [
        format_pval(welch_result.pvalue),
        format_pval(chi2_pval),
        "Effect size",
    ],
})

Markdown(inferential_summary.to_markdown(index=False))
```

::: {.card .summary-card}
Welch's one-way ANOVA tests whether average body mass differs among the three penguin species. Its p-value indicates whether the observed differences are statistically significant. The chi-square test examines whether species distribution is associated with island, while Cramer's V describes the strength of that association. A p-value below 0.05 is commonly treated as statistically significant.
:::

## Row {height=58%}

### Column

```{python}
#| title: "Body Mass Distribution by Species"
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| out-width: 100%
#| label: body-mass-boxplot

sns.set_style("whitegrid")
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4.5))

sns.boxplot(
    data=body_mass_clean,
    x="species",
    y="body_mass_g",
    hue="species",
    order=species_order,
    palette=palette,
    width=0.58,
    boxprops=dict(alpha=0.9, edgecolor="white"),
    medianprops=dict(color="white", linewidth=1.5),
    legend=True,
    ax=ax,
)

ax.set_xlabel("Penguin Species", fontweight="bold", fontsize=12)
ax.set_ylabel("Body Mass (grams)", fontweight="bold", fontsize=12)
ax.grid(axis="x", visible=False)
sns.despine(left=True, bottom=True)

handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
ax.legend(
    handles, labels, title="Species",
    title_fontproperties={"weight": "bold"},
    loc="upper center", bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.15), ncol=3, frameon=False
)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

::: {.card .summary-card}
The boxplot compares the distribution of body mass across species. The center line represents the median, while the box shows the middle 50% of observations. Differences in the medians and spreads help describe how body mass varies between species.
:::

### Column

```{python}
#| title: "Species Composition Across Islands"
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| out-width: 100%
#| label: species-island-proportions

species_island_props = (
    pd.crosstab(
        species_island_data["island"],
        species_island_data["species"],
        normalize="index",
    )
    .reindex(columns=species_order)
)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4.5))

species_island_props.plot(
    kind="bar",
    stacked=True,
    width=0.62,
    color=[palette[sp] for sp in species_order],
    edgecolor="white",
    linewidth=1,
    ax=ax,
)

ax.set_xlabel("Island", fontweight="bold", fontsize=12)
ax.set_ylabel("Percentage of Penguins", fontweight="bold", fontsize=12)
ax.set_ylim(0, 1.02)
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mtick.PercentFormatter(1.0))
ax.tick_params(axis="x", rotation=0)
ax.grid(axis="x", visible=False)
sns.despine(left=True, bottom=True)

ax.legend(
    title="Species",
    title_fontproperties={"weight": "bold"},
    loc="upper center", bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.15), ncol=3, frameon=False
)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

::: {.card .summary-card}
This proportional stacked bar chart compares the species composition of each island, with each bar representing 100% of the penguins recorded on that island. It makes differences in species distribution easier to compare even though the islands have different total numbers of observations.
:::
